# Black Women's Studies Minor (BSOS)
Source: https://academiccatalog.umd.edu/undergraduate/colleges-schools/behavioral-social-sciences/african-american-africana-studies/black-womens-studies-minor/
Source: https://wgss.umd.edu/
Source: https://aasd.umd.edu/
Source: https://arhu.umd.edu/undergraduate/academics/minors
Fetched: 2026-09-28

## Catalog requirements

Fifteen (15) credits of coursework are required, distributed below. No course with a grade less than "C-" may be used to satisfy the minor. An overall GPA of 2.0 in the minor is required for graduation. Students will design their program in consultation with the advisor in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies or African American Studies. No more than two courses may count toward a major in African American Studies or Women's Studies. Course lists can be found here: https://wgss.umd.edu/academic-programs/courses
Course | Title | Credits
Foundation Courses
Select one of the following: | 3
WGSS/AASP263 | Introduction to Black Women's Studies
WGSS/AASP265 | Constructions of Manhood and Womanhood in the Black Community
WGSS/AASP/LGBT264 | Quare/Queer Contentions: Exploration of Sexualities in the Black Community
Select one of the following: | 3
WGSS314/AASP313 | Black Women in United States History
HIST360 | Women and the Civil Rights Movement
AASP398 | Selected Topics in the African Diaspora (AASP389G: Gender, Labor, and Racial Identity in Diasporic Communities)
Electives | 9
Total Credits | 15
At least two electives must be at the 300 or 400 level.
One 300 or 400 level course must be Comparative or non-U.S.
See program for approved electives.

Dr. Shelbi Nahwilet Meissner and Dr. Diana Marsh (INFO)
The Harriet Tubman Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies at the University of Maryland offers comprehensive programs in undergraduate and graduate education, with a range of interdisciplinary programs and opportunities for students interested in exploring how the intersections of gender, race, sexuality, ethnicity, nationality, ability and other inequalities configure historical and contemporary struggles for social change.

The Indigenous Futures Lab
The Indigenous Futures Lab is a hub of Indigenous research, evaluation, and relationship-building where we center Indigenous knowledges to build futures of co-flourishing. Opened in October, 2023 the lab aims to co-create Indigenous futures through Indigenous-led scholarship and activism through engaging events and brand new research projects. To learn more about lab events and projects and get involved, visit the homepage by clicking the button below.

Undergraduate Studies
Minors are an excellent way for students to gain expertise in an area beyond the major. We encourage students to work with their advisors early to incorporate the minor into their Academic Plans.
Applications for all minors remain open until the minor is filled. Students will be taken on a first-come, first-served basis. When you click on the “contact form” below and select the appropriate option on the form, your request will be marked with the date and time. Please keep in mind that any pre-requisites must be completed by the time of application. (Students applying to the Music Performance minor must successfully pass an audition and should contact the advisor through the form below as soon as possible.)
When a minor is listed as CLOSED, it is closed until October 1 in the fall semester or March 1 in the spring semester. You may check this site again at these times. When a minor is listed as WAITLIST, it is closed, but you may put yourself on a waitlist by clicking on "contact form" below and selecting the appropriate option.
